decisions.why: The request (improvement 6) says 'run make quick after task-add' and FR-011 says task-add runs make quick's checks. Every check runs. decisions.summary: On a red, both files are restored to their pre-filing bytes, the checks are re-run, and failures (failed (exit N) plus each non-blank line, with only line/column numbers masked) are compared as multisets. decisions.why: This is FR-011 (withdraw and refuse, naming the failure, on a failure the new line introduces). The masking cannot hide a new failure: an identical message at a shifted line is still counted twice in the multiset, and only line/column digits are masked, so ids such as FR-023 and FR-024 stay distinct. The pre-existing case keeps the line, as FR-011 limits refusal to failures the new line introduces.

decisions.summary: A make -n quick that cannot list (no Makefile) refuses before anything is written.
decisions.why: Fails closed. Without a listing the requested check cannot run, so filing anyway would skip the enforcement the GM asked to be real. It adds no reach beyond FR-011.

decisions.summary: The escape reason must be two words and eight characters, else refused blocked/QUICK_OK-no-reason before anything is written.
decisions.why: FR-012 asks for 'a reason of two words or more'. Requiring eight characters as well makes the escape harder to use, which does not narrow the enforcement. The GM asked that enforcement be real (2026-11-19 approval).

decisions.why: Enforcement of FR-011 and FR-012's red-first requirement. Each test only fails when the requested behavior is absent.

decisions.summary: Found and left: the two real-tree probe rows in ~/.claude/guard-log and the rust/gate/CLAUDE.md task row not naming task_add/quick.rs are judged not defects.

decisions.why: It follows from D17's T20/T21 division; FR-010's 20 s bar is met by T21's splits, and SHARD_BAR_S is never a gate per D17.

decisions.summary: test-sync-with-main.sh is left whole (its split was built, measured and reverted); its full-run 26.8-40.2 s past the 20 s bar is now stated in found-and-left
decisions.why: Improvement 5's stated purpose (request.md) is that these suites 'set the floor on every make hooks-test', and the GM's 2026-11-20 words put the point as speed ('doing those first makes everything after them faster'). The block's measurements show the split defeats that purpose: full runs equal HEAD (mean 44.0 vs 43.9 s), the incremental run after a sync-with-main edit is slower with it split (12.7/12.1 s all-three vs 11.8/11.8 s l7r-gate alone), and its shards (8.7 + 7.7 + 4.0 s) cost more than the 5.0-7.7 s whole. It does not set the wall: re-read from the named logs /tmp/t21m/r1-4 and rm1-4-head-j8-c22.log, entry-gate finishes 10.1-14.8 s after it in every one of those eight runs, and its range 26.8-40.2 s matches them (40.2 is rm1, a run whose entry-gate took 51.5 s and which the entry-gate list drops as overlapped; without it 26.8-31.0 s - the stated range is the wider, not a hidden one). The earlier gap (SC-004's letter missed by a second suite, undisclosed) is closed: it is disclosed with figures and reasoning. Leaving a GUESS bar (D17) unmet with no wrong outcome is not a defect left (constitution XIV), so this is not deferral of a defect.

decisions.summary: test-entry-gate.sh is left whole, past the about-20 s bar in a full run (38.6-44.4 s); its case-4 chain of record gates is filed as its own performance task (T40, per the dispatch)
decisions.why: Same purpose test against request.md improvement 5. Splitting by its two cases does not lower the floor: full runs equal, and after an edit of it the split is slower (23.1/23.3 s vs 22.4/22.8 s whole); the wall is its case-4 chain, which a case split cannot shorten, and more job slots did not help. The literal split would ship a measured slowdown under the name of a speedup. The ruling rests on the chain being pursued as its own task so the request's purpose (entry-gate no longer setting the floor) is not dropped; the dispatch states it is filed as T40, an open [perf] box, which under FR-013 / SC-006 goes first. The 20 s bar is a GUESS, never a gate (D17); the request names no figure.

decisions.why: Implementation means of the split, following T20's shard form; changes no scope.

decisions.summary: Three pointers to test-l7r-gate.sh repointed to test-l7r-gate.3.sh; the seven to test-sync-with-main.sh left as the suite stays
decisions.why: Consequence of the kept split; the enumeration states its search (git grep of the three names).

decisions.summary: T20 builds and proves the shard form on test-parts.sh (split into test-parts.1.sh and test-parts.2.sh); the three slow suites, entry-gate.sh included, are split in T21, which lands before T22.
decisions.why: D17 in the accepted spec settles exactly this split of work: 'T20 builds the form, proved on test-parts.sh; T21 splits the three'. FR-010's three suites are all still split, by T21. The GM's 2026-11-20 order to do the improvements first is kept by T21 landing before T22. Nothing the GM asked for is dropped.

decisions.summary: A shard is tests/hooks/test-<name>.<k>.sh with k all digits, run in numeric order with gaps allowed. Each shard is its own job <guard>.<k> with its own .rc/.log/.s/.reads, and stamps nothing.
decisions.why: This is D17's 'treats each shard as a job', and the .s file is the place SC-004 measures. It is an implementation detail of FR-010 and narrows nothing.

decisions.summary: hookrun.sh --close stamps the suite once (its sha, its trace from every shard's reads, and its shard list .jobs), and only when every shard's job is ok. One red or missing shard leaves it unstamped.
decisions.why: This is D17's 'stamps the suite green when every shard is'.

decisions.summary: The recipe gives each shard its own key through deps --keys and hashes the guard's key with its shards' keys. A traced suite is skipped only while its shard list matches the kept .jobs, so an edited or added shard reruns the suite. No change to rust/guard.
decisions.why: This keeps D17's 'keyed by the suite's stamp key' and makes the skip correct for split suites. It is an implementation choice that narrows nothing.

decisions.summary: The GUARD WITHOUT A TEST check reads hookrun.sh --jobs once and accepts a guard's suite or its shards, including a single shard. It fails the run on SUITE AND SHARDS BOTH (a suite beside its own shards) and on SHARD WITHOUT ITS SUITE (a shard no rostered guard owns, which nothing would ever run).
decisions.why: D17 says the companion check 'accepts shards' and that a shard stands 'beside nothing else of that name'. SUITE AND SHARDS BOTH enforces that clause. SHARD WITHOUT ITS SUITE keeps a split from silently dropping cases, which is the plan's own constraint that every case still runs. Both only refuse a broken split of the requested kind and reach nothing else, so they enforce FR-010 and add no unrequested behavior.

decisions.summary: 16 new pins in test-parts.2.sh are proved red against HEAD's hookrun.sh. Done is measured by HOOKS_ALL=1 before and after runs and the shards' .s files. The plan expects no wall-time saving in T20 itself; the saving is T21's.
decisions.why: The tests only enforce the requested shard form. The measurement follows SC-004 and the GM's performance-first ruling (FR-013). Having T20 save nothing on its own follows from D17's split of work between T20 and T21.

decisions.summary: test-land-tooling.sh case 2b, a wall-clock assertion that failed once under load and passed on rerun, is left unfixed in T20 and handed to the launcher to file (DEFER_FORM_OK).
decisions.why: The GM never asked to fix this assertion and it is not part of FR-010, so leaving it narrows nothing he asked for. decisions.summary: Split tests/hooks/test-l7r-gate.sh into three shards (41 + 9 + 5 of its 55 checks), each making its own state
decisions.why: The split FR-010 / improvement 5 asks for, applied to one of the three named suites; every case still runs; shards 1.3/7.5/5.7 s alone, under the about-20 s bar; measured to save about 6 s of an incremental run.

decisions.summary: test-sync-with-main.sh is left whole (its split was built, measured and reverted)
decisions.why: Improvement 5's own stated purpose (request.md) is that these suites 'set the floor on every make hooks-test', and the GM's 2026-11-20 words put the point as speed ('makes everything after them faster'; prioritize performance). The block's own measurements show this split defeats that purpose concretely: it does not set any wall (entry-gate sets the full run's), full runs with all three split equal HEAD (mean 44.0 vs 43.9 s), the incremental run is slightly SLOWER with it split (12.7/12.1 s all-three-split vs 11.8/11.8 s l7r-gate-alone), and its shards cost 8.7 + 7.7 + 4.0 s against 5.0-7.7 s whole - the template run three times, added CPU on a host measured CPU-bound (11.6-12.5 cores busy). Not a cost or convenience argument: the split was implemented and reverted on measurement. Gap noted, not decisive: the found-and-left names only entry-gate past the 20 s bar and never states sync-with-main's full-run seconds whole (the next suite is about 10 s behind entry-gate's ~40 s), so a second miss of SC-004's letter may be undisclosed; it should be stated there.

decisions.summary: test-entry-gate.sh is left whole, past the about-20 s bar in a full run (38.6-44.4 s); its case-4 chain of record gates is filed as its own performance task
decisions.why: Same purpose test against request.md (improvement 5: 'sets the floor on every make hooks-test'). Splitting by its two cases does not lower the floor: full runs equal, and after an edit of it the split is slower (23.1/23.3 s vs 22.4/22.8 s whole); the wall is its case-4 chain, which a case split cannot shorten, and more job slots did not help either. Doing the literal split would ship a measured slowdown under the name of a speedup. This ruling rests on the chain being filed as its own task (the block: 'the chain itself is the lever, filed as its own task'), so the request's purpose - entry-gate no longer setting the floor - is still pursued rather than dropped; were that task not filed, the ruling would not hold. The 20 s bar is itself recorded as a GUESS, never a gate (D17), and the request names no figure.

decisions.summary: Shard helpers copied into each shard rather than sourced from a lib file, so l7r-guard deps keys them
decisions.why: Implementation means of the split, following T20's shard form; changes no scope.

decisions.why: Consequence of the kept split; stated with its search (git grep of the three names).
